CFML Language Reference: Functions

Evaluate

Takes each argument as a string, parses it as a CFML expression and evaluates it, from left to right. The value of the last expression is returned. This lets you build variable names and expressions at run time.

Category

Dynamic evaluation functions

Syntax

Evaluate(string_expression1 [, string_expression2 [, ... ] ])

Parameters

string_expression1
A string containing a CFML expression, for example "Price * Qty" or "Form.Answer#i#".
string_expression2...
More expressions. They are evaluated in order; only the last value is returned, so the earlier ones are useful for their side effects.

Returns

The value of the last expression evaluated.

Usage

The classic use is reading a variable whose name you only know at run time, such as numbered form fields: Evaluate("Form.Item#i#"). Note that the pound signs are resolved first, so the string handed to Evaluate is Form.Item1, Form.Item2, and so on.

If a string is not a valid expression, an Expression exception is thrown. Never pass raw user input to Evaluate: anything the visitor types would be run as CFML. To set a variable with a computed name, use SetVariable; to get a literal string through an evaluation, use DE.

Example

Opens the example in a new window. The example runs on this server, so it only works when you browse from the server itself (127.0.0.1).
<!--- three "form fields" with numbered names --->
<CFSET Item1 = "56K modem">
<CFSET Item2 = "Netscape 4.7 CD">
<CFSET Item3 = "Y2K patch">
<UL>
<CFLOOP INDEX="i" FROM="1" TO="3">
  <CFOUTPUT><LI>Item#i# = #Evaluate("Item#i#")#</CFOUTPUT>
</CFLOOP>
</UL>
<CFSET Formula = "Len(Item1) * 2 + 1">
<CFOUTPUT>
<P>Evaluate("#Formula#") = #Evaluate(Formula)#
<P>Evaluate("Total = 10", "Total * 3") = #Evaluate("Total = 10", "Total * 3")#
</CFOUTPUT>

See also

DE, IIf, SetVariable, IsDefined
